summary: Resumed from rebuild 4 (the committed pose: IoU 0.964, contour p95 4.24 px, only p95 failing). Two things about that pose were fixed. (1) Anatomy. Its phalanx lengths had drifted up to +17 % from the step-2 start pose (index +17/+15/+15 %, middle P1 -13 %, thumb metacarpal -14 %). New fits (a surrogate of build_hands.py's own SDF, Levenberg-Marquardt on the edge offset at every reference edge pixel, counting only error beyond 1.2 px, plus a per-region thickness balance) now keep every 3D phalanx within +-10 % of the start pose. Two exceptions: the index middle and distal phalanges follow the reference keypoints, which the start pose had 12-15 % short, and the pinky's middle and distal phalanges keep the previous run's anatomical-ratio fix. (2) The fingers are fuller where the drawing is fuller: the ring changed from 82 px net too thin to 28 px fuller, the thumb from -166 to -110 px, the middle from -42 to -22 px. The index went from +17 to -44 px. Two changes were tried and rejected. When the dorsal vector was left free it drifted 33 deg for almost no silhouette gain, so it stays at [0.4, 0.86, 0.32]. Freeing the wrist and palm z/flat gave the best p95 (4.00, rebuild 5), but the above view showed the carpus flared into a wide, thin wedge (palm-end half-width 147 px against 113-120 px), so z, flat and dorsal are all back at the start values. Fingertip px were set with scratch Blender builds, because the surrogate's tips are 1-2 px off Blender's. Final state = rebuild 6 (with --views): IoU 0.9627, mean 1.69, p95 4.12, neg 0.915. All tips, all 16 joints, A1 and D9 pass. Only contour p95 fails (4.12 px against 2.0). The run stopped on the plateau rule: no Blender build improved p95 in 9 consecutive builds after rebuild 5. The residual is mostly shapes the builder cannot make. The index knuckle bump plus its step down (110 of the 245 edge px over 4 px), the wrist bump/notch, the wrist crease and palm heel, and the sag of the forearm's dorsal line account for 231 of those 245 px. p95 falls a level only when at most 212 remain. Rebuilds: 6 into the repo (1-4 previous run, 5-6 this run) plus 15 scratch Blender builds in /tmp/calib-left/builder*/ (7 previous, 8 this run) = 21.

openIssues: The index MCP sits 26 px (2.63u, gate 3u) up-left of its reading and the index PIP 13 px (2.22u) back from its reading. In this builder the knuckle bump can only come from the metacarpal head at the MCP centre, so that is where the drawn bump pulls the MCP; the +-10 % length limit then pushes the PIP back. Once the knuckle can protrude (builder request 1), move the MCP back toward (592,306) and the PIP onto (682,344).

Middle and ring fingers: 3D P2/P1 = 0.87 and 0.94, against about 0.6-0.7 anatomically. The start pose had the same (0.86 / 0.95): their proximal phalanges are foreshortened in the drawing, and the reconstructed depth keeps them nearly in the image plane (see decision 2).

The pose-level remainder is 2-4 px along the index, the back of the hand and the D5 slit (the render slit is 5-6 px wider on its upper left). Net thickness against the drawing: thumb -110 px (partly that slit), index -44, pinky -39, middle -22, ring +28.

The middle and ring tips pass with little margin (3.16 and 3.61 px against 4.0). The tip rule jumps by whole pixels, and the surrogate's tips differ from Blender's by 1-2 px, so any later change to the pose or the builder must re-check them in Blender. The index tip is exactly on the reference tip (0 px), for the contact gap.
D9 is fragile at the D5 slit bottom (557-559, 418-419): a 1 px ring-tip move made it fail in a scratch build (t6v3). The final pose passes.
wrist>palm is 18 % shorter than in the start pose. The palm joint is only the carpus construction point, moved about 50 px toward the wrist by the previous run's fits and kept there.
The forearm cuff past the frame is visible in the side and top views (known step-3 item).

builderRequests: Knuckle prominence (the largest residual). The MCP knuckle ellipsoid never reaches the silhouette: its dorsal extent is about N_head (centre lifted knuckle_lift 0.5 x N_head, half-axis an = 0.8 x knuckle_size 0.62 x N_head), which is the metacarpal head's own surface. The proximal phalanx also starts with the full MCP section (the head is only meta_head 1.12x larger), so the drawn index-knuckle bump and its ~11 px step down to the finger cannot form. Numbers: 180 of 207 edge px > 2 px at x 520-640, y 215-310, and 110 of the hand's 245 edge px > 4 px (they alone keep p95 at about 4.1). The fitters compensate by moving the index MCP 26 px (2.6u) off its reading. Request: let the knuckle protrude about 0.3-0.4 x N_head beyond the head (e.g. knuckle_lift about 0.9 or a larger dorsal half-axis), and/or narrow the proximal phalanx base relative to the head, so a pose can keep the MCP at its reading and still draw the bump and the step. Evidence: outputs/qa/calib/compare-left/residual-knuckle.png, residual-primitives.png.

Wrist-to-back notch at (357-362, 175-179), max 9.4 px: the concave junction between the carpus's steep dorsal edge and the index metacarpal's rounded base cap (meta_base_frac 0.30). The k_body 0.045 blend fills only part of it, while the drawn dorsal line is straight there; it also shows as a kink in the shaded home view. Request: start the fan nearer the wrist, or blend the carpus's dorsal edge into the index metacarpal line (a larger k at that junction, or a dorsal carpus profile). Evidence: residual-wrist.png, residual-primitives.png.

Forearm profile and wrist bump: the forearm is a single elliptic cone with straight silhouette edges. The drawn dorsal forearm line sags about 4.5 px between x 48 and 256 (the best straight line still leaves 2.4-2.7 px), and a separate dorsal wrist bump (ulnar head, x 285-310) stands 2-3 px above the render. Numbers: forearm top 236 of 466 edge px > 2 px, wrist bump/notch 108 of 200. Request: an optional mid-forearm control (a third arm joint or a sag parameter) and a dorsal wrist prominence. Evidence: residual-forearm.png, residual-wrist.png.

Wrist crease and palm heel on the underside: k_arm 0.060 (about 29 px) rounds away the drawn concave wrist crease (render 3-4 px outside at x 285-320, y 255-290), and no primitive gives the palm heel below it its own convex mass (render 3-5 px inside at x 320-367, y 290-335). Numbers: 129 of 192 edge px > 2 px. Request: a smaller underside blend at the wrist and a palm-heel mass a pose can size. Evidence: residual-wrist.png.

Palm width coupling: the carpus's palm-end section and the metacarpal fan's base thickness (meta_thick x the palm's N) both come from the palm joint's r and flat. So the one pose lever that fits the palm block's silhouette best (palm flat 0.45 -> 0.337, rebuild 5, p95 4.00) also widens the carpus to a 147 px half-width, a flared wedge seen from above (start pose 120, rebuild 4 113). Request: cap the carpus width near half the knuckle span, or give the fan base a thickness independent of the palm section. Evidence: /tmp/calib-left/r5/above-rb4-vs-rb5.png, /tmp/calib-left/r5/rb5-views.png.
Existing step-3 item, unchanged: remove the forearm cuff past the frame (visible in the side and top views).

decisionsForUser.question: The left contour-p95 gate (2.0 px, D14) cannot be reached by editing the pose. After 21 Blender builds and a surrogate search, the best acceptable pose sits at 4.12 px. Most of the error is shapes build_hands.py cannot make: the index knuckle bump and its step, the wrist notch and bump, the wrist crease and palm heel, and the sag of the forearm's dorsal line. Per D6 the gate stays. How should the left hand go on?
options: (a) Do the builder changes in step 3 first (knuckle prominence, wrist-to-back junction, forearm profile and wrist bump, wrist crease and palm heel, palm-width decoupling; see builderRequests), then re-run step-2 calibration of the left hand against the same gates. Fixing the knuckle alone removes about 110 of the 245 edge px over 4 px. Reaching p95 <= 2 px would also need about 1000 of the 1276 edge px now over 2 px to come within 2 px, which is not guaranteed.
(b) Accept the recorded left residual (p95 4.12 px; every other left gate passes) and go on to steps 3-5 without recalibrating the left hand.

Edge px over 4 px: 245 in total; knuckle 110, palm heel 49, wrist bump/notch 44, forearm top 28, D5 slit 10; p95 drops only once at most 212 remain. Crops: outputs/qa/calib/compare-left/residual-knuckle.png, residual-wrist.png, residual-forearm.png, residual-slit.png, residual-hand.png, residual-primitives.png. Log: /tmp/calib-left/iterations.md.
decisionsForUser.recommendation: (a): the residual is mostly builder vocabulary, not pose. Do the knuckle and wrist-junction changes first; they remove most of the tail over 4 px. Then re-run step 2 for the left hand and report again.
decisionsForUser.blocks: Closing step 2 for the left hand (the contour-p95 gate). The pose and assets on disk are consistent (rebuild 6) and can be used by steps 4-5 meanwhile.

decisionsForUser.question: The curled middle and ring fingers have implausible 3D proportions: their middle phalanx is almost as long as the proximal one (P2/P1 = 0.87 and 0.94; about 0.6-0.7 in a real finger). The start pose already had this. Their proximal phalanges are foreshortened in the drawing (72-75 px projected), and the reconstructed depth keeps them almost in the image plane (z 0.06 -> 0.05 and -0.05 -> -0.06). Making them anatomical needs a depth reading that one view does not settle. Should their PIPs be moved in depth?
options: (a) Keep the reconstructed depth (silhouette unchanged, proportions as now).

(b) Move the middle and ring PIPs away from the camera (palmar flexion at the MCP, about 0.10-0.15 world units) so that P1 is about 1.4-1.6 x P2 in 3D. The home silhouette barely changes; the ±35°/above views and which digit hides which do.
(c) Move them toward the camera instead (the finger rising toward the viewer before it curls down).

decisionsForUser.recommendation: (b): palmar flexion is the anatomical direction for these curled fingers (the palm faces down and slightly away from the camera). Do it together with the step-3 rebuild and check it in the ±35° and above views. It does not block anything in step 2.
